C1.rationale: Level 2 anchor: 'At least one core unit assesses collaborative practice — group projects with individual accountability, client or stakeholder work, interprofessional activity.' Two core units document assessed group work: BUSA90520 (Data Wrangling and Visualisation) runs three graded group tasks, and ECOM90025 (Advanced Data Analysis) runs a graded group case competition/presentation and a group empirical project. Level 3 additionally requires an assessment where 'the division of work between people and systems is itself assessed' — no core assessment documents coordinating work across people AND tools/AI systems, so the item stops at 2.

C2.rationale: Level 0 anchor: 'No assessment requires students to appraise the quality of work — their own, peers', or a tool's.' The captured core-unit assessment breakdowns (BUSA90520, ECOM90001, ECOM90002, ECOM90024, ECOM90025) consist entirely of proposal/progress/submission reports, individual and group assignments, quizzes and hurdle examinations — none framed as peer review, structured critique, exemplar-based marking or a documented reliance-on-tool/source justification. No 'reflection', 'self-assessment' or 'peer review' language appears anywhere in the extract, so Level 1's outcome-only reflection language is also absent.

C3.rationale: Level 1 anchor: 'AI or digital tools appear only as electives or as tool operation/training — the operational level TEQSA identifies as non-durable.' Core units document digital-tool operation training — computer software use for estimation and graphing, statistical software for time-series handling, computational methods for data preparation — but nothing in the extract names AI specifically or discusses limitations, ethics or governance. Per the Migration note ('tool-operation content caps at level 1'), this content caps the item at 1 regardless of appearing in core rather than elective subjects; Levels 2–3 require AI-specific limitations/ethics or governance content, which is absent.

C4.rationale: Level 2 anchor: 'At least one core assessment requires application to novel or unfamiliar problems — case variation, unseen datasets, cross-context projects.' Two core units (ECOM90001, ECOM90002) each assess a staged project requiring students to formulate their own hypotheses and collect real-world data rather than work a taught example — an unseen/self-selected dataset applied outside the worked-example content. Level 3 requires 'a self-scoped capstone or research project' with documented structured progression; ECOM90002 titles its assessment items 'Capstone Project Proposal/Progress/Submission', which gestures toward this, but the program's actual designated Capstone subjects (Year 2: ECOM90026/ECOM90027 Econometrics Research Report, ECOM90013 Econometrics 3) have no captured evidence in this extract, so a documented progression to an independent capstone cannot be confirmed. Ambiguity resolved to the lower level.

C5.rationale: Level 2 anchor: 'Students design and conduct an inquiry with methodology selection and data collection, assessed.' ECOM90001 and ECOM90002 both assess a staged research/capstone project in which students formulate hypotheses, select methodology and collect real-world data, submitted as graded proposal/progress/submission reports. Level 3 requires the primary-evidence project to be 'REQUIRED (not one route among several)' with methodology 'defended under scrutiny (viva, defence, or staged supervised review)'. The program's dedicated Capstone subjects — where a defence/viva component would most plausibly sit — have no subject or assessment pages captured in this extract, so that requirement cannot be confirmed from the available evidence.

The three placement-type subjects in the course structure — Business Practicum, Global Business Practicum, Business and Economics Internship — appear only inside the Year 2 elective lists, explicitly as one optional choice among several requiring Program Director approval. G1.rationale: DEMOTED on verify pass: the submitted rationale claimed 'an explicit staged prerequisite chain between core subjects', but a full-text search of the extract finds exactly ONE prerequisite relationship in the entire 2,245-line document — ECOM90013 (Econometrics 3) as a concurrent prerequisite for ECOM90026 (Econometrics Research Report Part 1) — and both subjects are alternative Capstone options, not core subjects. One link is not a 'chain'. The other two PASS routes are also unsupported: the core is not all-compulsory (one of the six core slots is selected from ECOM90003/ECOM90004/ECON90033, and the Capstone slot is selected from ECOM90026/ECOM90013), and no accreditation is mentioned anywhere. PASS may still be defensible on the gate's primary criterion — a documented foundational-to-advanced core sequence (Data Wrangling/Basic Econometrics → Econometrics 2/Advanced Data Analysis/Forecasting → Capstone) — but that is not the ground the original rationale cited, so as justified it is not supported by the evidence quoted. Recorded as FAIL pending re-grounding in subject-sequence progression rather than the unsupported 'chain' claim.
